title: The Combination Clause
question: What, concretely, redeems "mere combination" — and what is being called a combination in the first place?

figures.title: The redemptions: what would make a combination count
figures.deck: Six distinct ways out, holding 76% of the clause's own sentences — added value, new insight, differentiation, a new mechanism, an isolated contribution, innovation beyond the integration — and two clauses that offer none.

claims.statement: Six genuine exception clauses hold 76% of the combination rule's own sentences.
claims.derivation: sum of .share over the six non-dead-end exceptions (excludes "The threshold, restated" and "The reproduction floor")

claims.statement: 24% of statements offer no exit — two dead-end tracks ("the threshold, restated" and "the reproduction floor") that never rejoin the main line.
claims.derivation: 1 - sum(.share over the six genuine exceptions) = 1 - 0.7595

claims.statement: An explicit conditional word (unless, without, only if) appears in 43.6% of the combination-rule statements — a floor, since track families are read from a sentence's content rather than its grammar.
claims.derivation: count of the 4,316 combination-rule sentences containing an explicit conditional marker / 4,316

figures.title: The referents: what is being called a combination
figures.deck: In 46% of charges the assembled parts are never named: the reviewer says the work combines existing methods without saying which.

claims.statement: 46% of combination charges assemble no named parts at all.
claims.derivation: referents entry 'The generic combination charge'.share, over the 4,262 combination-rule units

claims.statement: 18% of combination charges recite the parts' names.
16% of combination charges match one specific named precedent.
claims.derivation: referents entry for the named-precedent-match cluster, .share

claims.statement: 12% of combination charges concede the problem is new and charge only the tools, and 8% charge precisely the absence of a new insight.
claims.derivation: referents entries for the new-problem-conceded and no-new-insight clusters, .share each

caveats.text: Clusters are data-driven (k-means over sentence embeddings); merges and names are readings of exemplars drafted by a machine reader and reviewed by the analyst. Raw clusters ship with the dataset.
caveats.scope: Fig. 8a exception-clause shares and Fig. 8b referent shares

caveats.text: The 46% generic-charge share is measured on the distilled observations, so it was audited against the source reviews: in a 30-case sample, wherever the source charge could be located, its specificity matched the observation's — with one ambiguous exception — so the share is not an artifact of summarization.
